reasoning: The core problem — a static/deterministic pre-execution firewall over agent tool calls that blocks harmful/irreversible actions while measuring benign-task breakage — is substantially solved. AEGIS (arXiv 2603.12621) interposes on the tool-execution path with composable policy validation, blocking 100% of 48 attacks at a 1.2% false-positive rate on 500 benign calls, which is exactly the harm-blocked-vs-benign-broken measurement proposed. "Enforcing Benign Trajectories: A Behavioral Firewall" (arXiv 2604.26274) compiles benign tool-call telemetry into a deterministic automaton of permitted sequences/parameter bounds, and Praetor learns deterministic firewall rules from clean traces (cutting attack success 12.8%→2.2%); LlamaFirewall, AgentSpec, and the "Irreversibility Budget" runtime-governance line all enforce pre-execution deterministic rules classified by irreversibility. The one genuine gap is the proposal's specific framing — a greedy/coverage search for the *minimal* high-coverage rule set on the harm-vs-breakage frontier evaluated on SHADE-Arena/CUA-SHADE sabotage traces as an explicit cheap baseline floor — which no single found paper does directly, though firewall rule-set minimization is itself a classic problem (CrossRef: "Reducing the Size of Rule Set in a Firewall").

evidence.title: AEGIS: No Tool Call Left Unchecked — A Pre-Execution Firewall and Audit Layer for AI Agents
evidence.summary: Pre-execution firewall interposing on the tool-execution path with deep argument extraction, content-first risk scanning, and composable policy validation. Blocks all 48 curated attacks before execution at a 1.2% false-positive rate on 500 benign tool calls with 8.3ms median latency. This is essentially the harm-blocked-vs-benign-broken evaluation of a static tool-call policy engine the proposal describes.

evidence.title: Enforcing Benign Trajectories: A Behavioral Firewall for Structured-Workflow AI Agents
evidence.summary: Compiles verified benign tool-call telemetry into a parameterized deterministic finite automaton defining permitted tool sequences, contexts, and parameter bounds — directly the idea of deriving a deterministic rule-based firewall from benign vs harmful agent traces.

evidence.title: Praetor: A firewall that learns from clean agent traces cuts attack success from 12.8% to 2.2%
evidence.summary: Deterministic agent firewall built from clean (benign) trajectories that substantially reduces attack success rate, reflecting the same trace-driven harm-vs-breakage firewall framing proposed.

evidence.title: LlamaFirewall: An open source guardrail system for building secure AI agents
evidence.summary: Production guardrail system (Meta) including a deterministic static-analysis component (CodeShield) and policy guardrails over agent actions; establishes that low-overhead pre-execution guardrails balancing security and benign utility are an active, well-developed area.

evidence.title: Runtime Governance for AI Agents: Policies on Paths / Irreversibility Budget
evidence.summary: Classifies each tool call by irreversibility on a standardized scale and enforces preemptive prevention rather than post-hoc recording, covering the 'block irreversible actions via runtime rules' framing the proposal targets.

evidence.title: Reducing the Size of Rule Set in a Firewall
evidence.summary: Classic networking work on minimizing firewall rule sets; the proposal's distinctive minimal-rule-set/coverage-search angle is a well-studied optimization problem, just not yet applied to LLM-agent sabotage traces.
